verdicts.reason: Stated directly; structural but testable by access scenarios.
Interface description only; nothing specific to verify beyond the bus parameters.
Stated, but o_regs equal to register value is observable via interface; scenario is better since the register value is internal, only checkable via write/readback.
Address map of R/W registers is stated and testable.
Reset value 0 is stated; checkable via o_regs and scenario.
Byte-lane write strobes stated; testable by scenario.
Sampling timing of i_status at read address handshake is stated.
The block must accept all orderings; it is a slave requirement, not master optional behaviour.
Block must support concurrent read and write; slave requirement.
Fixed latency stated and checkable on interface signals each cycle.
Combinational independence of outputs from inputs is not checkable as a per-cycle interface assertion; verify by scenario/structure. Registered outputs are better tested with scenarios.
Clock and async active-low reset stated.
Never produces EXOKAY/DECERR; checkable on every response.
Prot signals ignored; stated and testable.

questions.question: Does 'one cycle' latency mean the response is asserted in the next cycle after the handshake, and does it hold when bready/rready is low (stall)? Also what is 'last write handshake' when AW and W arrive at different times?
On an unmapped write, are register contents unchanged, and what happens with a partly mapped address range (addresses 0x00+4k beyond PARA_NUM_REGS up to 0x40)?
Does a write to the status register at 0x40 return SLVERR or OKAY?
